summary: Ferry County, WA, DNR site: first lookout 1934, current 15-ft DNR live-in cab built 1986 (old L-4 cab moved to Molson Museum); last staffed 1995.

facts.design: 15-foot tower with DNR live-in cab (built 1986); the L-4 cab that stood on it earlier is now at the Molson Museum

access.note: On state forest land at the end of a gravel road with a gate near the top (TrailChick, 2017). No current DNR access notice found, and nothing says the cab itself is open to visitors.

visit.trail_note: High-clearance 4x4 needed; 4WD required in wet or snowy weather; road narrow and deeply rutted in places; room to park a few cars at the summit.

events.note: First lookout developed with an L-5 cab (NHLR; TrailChick lists site established 1934)
Aircraft Warning Service site, March 27 to October 5, 1942 (Seattle Filter Center)
October 7, 1944 Colville Examiner item names Alevida Webb of Ellensburg on Franson Peak
Current 15-ft tower with DNR live-in cab built (NHLR 'Built' field; TrailChick 'Current Structure Built')
The older L-4 cab moved to the Molson Museum when the current structure went up
Registered April 11, 2022, nominated by Christine Estrada

corrections.proposed: 15-foot tower with DNR live-in cab (built 1986); the L-4 cab that stood on an earlier 15-foot tower is at the Molson Museum
corrections.why: The L-4 cab belongs to the 1950s structure and was moved to Molson when the 1986 structure went up. The summit record should describe the current DNR live-in cab.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1934 is the first lookout (L-5 cab) and 1986 is the current structure. The brief's 1986 is the current structure's date; the story gives both.

NHLR says the site is Washington State Forest Land administered by the DNR. TrailChick's 2017 listing gives Colville National Forest as the land. The story follows NHLR, which names the administering agency.

notes_for_editor: Access is the weak point. Only TrailChick (visited 2017) and Huckleberry Press (April 2022) describe the road, and no DNR notice was found. The level is restricted because of the gate and because nothing says the cab is open. The 1950s replacement is given as 'the 1950s' with no event year. The 1942 AWS dates come from NHLR and the Rex's page. Coordinates in the brief (48.855779, -118.632521) are within about 10 m of TrailChick's (48.855745, -118.632588). Two other pages (firelookout.com and ramblr.com) were seen in search results but not read. Read budget: five pages and one search.
